attack_post_unresolved_questions: No supplied evidence quantifies the deployed effectiveness of the cited CISA CPG or NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 brute-force mitigation controls (failed-login lockout, unique credentials, MFA, delay algorithms).

The PMT NoP publication-activity trend is supported by E_33_A707006877BFD1C2 but is explicitly limited to publication activity; it does not establish deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, or causal mitigation effectiveness, so it cannot resolve whether IDS/IPS will materially change realized brute-force outcomes.

The supplied evidence does not include an exploitation_signal slot or a direct temporal measure of brute-force incident count/frequency, so the forecast's threat NoI increasing direction cannot be confirmed or challenged from the surfaced evidence.

There is no supplied evidence comparing the rate of change in brute-force NoI with the rate of change in IDS/IPS NoP publication activity, so the forecasted threat-minus-PMT gap direction and the 2025 negative versus 2026-2027 positive gap values cannot be validated.
defense_post_unresolved_questions: How the recommended account-protection, MFA, and credential-hygiene controls from CISA CPG and NIST SP 800-53 would interact with or substitute for IDS/IPS in this Threat–PMT pair is not quantified in the payload.

No surfaced evidence provides a temporal measure of brute-force incident count or frequency (NoI) for 2025–2027, so the forecast's threat-side increasing direction and the signed gap movement (−0.342 in 2025 to +0.334 in 2026, +0.328 in 2027) cannot be independently validated from the evidence boundary.

The exploitation_signal slot remains missing from the surfaced evidence set, so the payload does not directly show live exploitation or attack-success trends for brute force relative to IDS/IPS in the 2025–2027 window.

Whether IDS/IPS publication activity (NoP) translates into 2025–2027 deployment, adoption, or operational effectiveness for brute-force defense is not directly evidenced; the Crossref trend record explicitly disclaims any such linkage.

final_mediator_adjudications.rationale: Both critics now converge on the evidentiary limitation in E_03_F2B2EBA86BEEFDC5. The Attack critic (Round 2 response to C7) explicitly acknowledges that 'the 10% stolen-credentials figure is chart-derived with ambiguous label-to-value mapping and should be qualified' and that 'C7 framing resolves my concern.' The Defense critic (Round 2 response to A2) maintains that 'until that qualification is incorporated, A2 remains REVISE.' The chart-value sequence in E_03_F2B2EBA86BEEFDC5 ('38 %17 % 10 % 6 % 3 % 2 % 1 % 1 % 2 % 15 % 5 %') does not align with the category listing order (the narrative-confirmed 15% prior-compromise appears as the 10th value, not the 3rd), making the 10%-to-stolen-credentials mapping ambiguous. The narrative confirms exploit=38%, phishing=17%, prior-compromise=15%; the 6% brute-force and 10% stolen-credentials figures are chart-derived. Both critics agree on the substance; the revision is mechanical and must appear in the final post-assessment.
final_mediator_adjudications.required_revision: In the final post-assessment for A2: (1) retain the 6% brute-force figure and the narrative-confirmed 38% exploit, 17% phishing, 15% prior-compromise comparisons; (2) explicitly note that the 10% stolen-credentials figure is derived from chart data in E_03_F2B2EBA86BEEFDC5 whose label-to-value ordering is ambiguous in the extracted text and is not confirmed by the narrative paragraph; (3) present the 6% brute-force figure as the most contextually anchored chart-derived value; (4) do not present the 10% as having the same evidentiary basis as the narrative-confirmed figures. Preserve NEUTRAL_CONTEXT relation.

final_mediator_adjudications.rationale: Both critics now REVISE the opponent's forecast_relation label for the same evidence (E_03_C54C5F099169E020). The Attack critic REVISEs C6, stating that 'the claim as written with CHALLENGES_FORECAST is not directly grounded: the chunk records observed adversary behavior, not a temporal NoI trend, control-effectiveness measurement, or gap outcome.' The Defense critic REVISEs A3, stating that 'these are observed operational behaviors at a point in time and do not measure a temporal increase in brute-force incident count or frequency' and that 'with a generic SUPPORTS_FORECAST relation, A3 remains too broad.' The evidence in E_03_C54C5F099169E020 documents observed adversary behaviors (password guessing against cloud sign-in portals, SIM swapping, social engineering, MFA push notification abuse, help-desk abuse) at a point in time. It contains no temporal measure of brute-force incident count or frequency in either the increasing or decreasing direction, and no quantification of control effectiveness. Neither SUPPORTS_FORECAST (A3) nor CHALLENGES_FORECAST (C6) is grounded; the appropriate framing is neutral operational context for brute-force credential-targeting persistence.
final_mediator_adjudications.required_revision: For A3 (Attack): retain the factual description of observed adversary behaviors from E_03_C54C5F099169E020 but change the forecast_relation from SUPPORTS_FORECAST to NEUTRAL_CONTEXT, explicitly stating that these behaviors support the operational context of brute-force credential-targeting persistence but do not constitute direct evidence of a temporal NoI incident-count or frequency increase. For C6 (Defense): retain the factual description from E_03_C54C5F099169E020 but change the forecast_relation from CHALLENGES_FORECAST to NEUTRAL_CONTEXT, explicitly stating that these observed behaviors document adversary capability and persistence but do not measure control effectiveness, temporal NoI change, or gap outcome. Both claims should be read as observed adversary behavior context, not as directional forecast support or challenge.

final_mediator_adjudications.rationale: The Attack critic (Round 2 response to C8) now explicitly states: 'This is neutral operational context for brute-force facilitation conditions; it does not provide a direct temporal NoI incident-count or frequency trend for brute force and does not validate the forecast gap.' The Defense critic (Round 2 response to A4) maintains that A4 'remains too broad' with its SUPPORTS_FORECAST relation and requires explicit reframing. Both critics agree on the substance: E_04_02D425B67E57F323 documents OT-related vulnerability-scanning context (older vulnerabilities, widespread scanning, brute-force facilitation conditions) as a point-in-time operational landscape, not a temporal NoI trend. The Stage 1 A4 claim's SUPPORTS_FORECAST label is not supported by the evidence content. The revision is agreed in substance; it must be incorporated in the final post-assessment.
final_mediator_adjudications.required_revision: In the final post-assessment for A4: retain the factual description from E_04_02D425B67E57F32D (older vulnerabilities and widespread scanning in OT-related industries, vulnerabilities that can make brute-force attacks easier) but change the forecast_relation from SUPPORTS_FORECAST to NEUTRAL_CONTEXT, explicitly stating that the OT vulnerability-scanning and older-threat-relevance context supports operational awareness of conditions that can facilitate brute-force attacks but does not provide a direct temporal NoI incident-count or frequency trend for brute force. Do not present as independent validation of the threat NoI increasing direction.

final_mediator_adjudications.rationale: The Attack critic REVISEs C4 on two grounds. First, citation completeness: C4's statement mentions 'MFA' as part of the described controls, but C4's evidence_ids (E_23_B21FAA9377991F05, E_23_EBCAB9508641E703, E_25_FE58E4FCF044EDE3) do not include E_23_312B9513BCEE9B9D, which is the CISA CPG record containing the MFA options and IT/OT MFA recommendations. E_23_B21FAA9377991F05 covers failed-login alerting/lockout (PR.AC-7), E_23_EBCAB9508641E703 covers unique credentials (PR.AC-1), and E_25_FE58E4FCF044EDE3 covers NIST unsuccessful-logon lockout/delay. The MFA component is grounded only in E_23_312B9513BCEE9B9D. Second, forecast role: C4's CHALLENGES_FORECAST label overstates the evidentiary contribution. The cited records are official recommended-control mappings (CISA CPG, NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5) that do not quantify operational effectiveness, deployment maturity, or realized brute-force mitigation performance. They do not directly evidence that the forecast gap will be challenged. The Defense critic's own stance_basis does not list C4 as a challenging claim, indicating the CHALLENGES_FORECAST label is not load-bearing in the Defense position.
final_mediator_adjudications.required_revision: In the final post-assessment for C4: (1) add E_23_312B9513BCEE9B9D to the evidence_ids list to properly support the MFA component mentioned in the statement, or remove the MFA reference if that evidence is not to be cited; (2) change the forecast_relation from CHALLENGES_FORECAST to NEUTRAL_CONTEXT, explicitly stating that the cited CISA CPG and NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 records describe recommended account-protection, unique-credential, MFA, failed-login alerting, lockout, and delay controls mapped to brute-force techniques, and that these are official control-mapping context rather than quantified effectiveness evidence or direct evidence challenging the forecast direction.

final_mediator_adjudications.rationale: Round 2 resolves the interpretive dispute from Round 1's UNRESOLVED stance adjudication. The Defense critic explicitly clarifies (FOCUS-R2-STANCE responses to A9 and A10) that 'the Defense rationale is anchored to this PMT NoP publication evidence and does not require implicit acceptance of a directly evidenced temporal increase in brute-force NoI incident count or frequency' and that 'this limitation qualifies the weight of A9/C1 for any overall gap interpretation, but it does not negate the supported PMT NoP publication direction.' The Attack critic explicitly concedes (Round 2 responses to C1 and C2) that E_33_A707006877BFD1C2 'directly reports the 2021-2024 IDS/IPS publication counts and OLS slope and supports a directional PMT NoP publication trajectory' but maintains this 'does not establish threat NoI temporal increase, deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, or the signed threat-minus-PMT gap.' Both critics now agree on: (a) the PMT NoP publication-activity trajectory is supported by E_33_A707006877BFD1C2; (b) the publication trend explicitly does not establish deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, or causal mitigation effectiveness; (c) no temporal NoI incident-count or frequency trend for brute force exists in the surfaced evidence; (d) the signed gap values cannot be independently validated. The stances reflect different emphases on different forecast components: Defense's SUPPORT_DOMINANCE addresses the PMT NoP component, Attack's NO_DIRECTIONAL_EVIDENCE addresses the threat NoI component. These are not mutually exclusive and both are grounded within the surfaced evidence boundary.

Both critics agree in Round 2 on the factual content and NEUTRAL_CONTEXT framing of E_02_669F59880AF52688: 1,997 basic web application attack incidents, 881 with confirmed data disclosure, and the stated credential-abuse pattern (brute forcing, buying, reusing default/simplistic/guessable credentials). Both correctly note this is point-in-time observed threat context, not a temporal NoI incident-count or frequency trend. No substantive dispute.

Both critics agree in Round 2 that the three Crossref metadata records (E_29_8E495DC2A98305B1, E_29_BAD6581A8E96027C, E_29_CA00E63DF08305B1) support the described IDS/IPS technical-literature topics (DoS/DDoS efficiency, Suricata in IDS/IPS modes, IDS/IPS with Telegram notification). Both correctly note these are publication metadata and technical-literature context, not deployment maturity or operational effectiveness evidence. No substantive dispute.

The Defense critic agrees in Round 2 with both A5 and A6. A5 correctly describes the CISA CPG mapping of brute-force techniques (T1110.001-T1110.004) to failed-login alerting/lockout (E_23_B21FAA9377991F05), unique credentials (E_23_EBCAB9508641E703), and MFA (E_23_312B9513BCEE9B9D). A6 correctly describes the NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 unsuccessful-logon-attempt controls including automatic account lockout or delay algorithms (E_25_FE58E4FCF044EDE3). Both are properly framed as NEUTRAL_CONTEXT operational mitigation context. No dispute on these specific claims.

Both critics agree (Defense Round 2 response to A7) that E_12_D8076704AE363FE2 supports the description of MITRE ATT&CK M1029 remote data storage and log-forwarding measures, including forwarding IDS/IPS logs to a remote security information system, as protective measures for security logs and monitoring data. Both note this is mitigation-implementation context, not operational effectiveness evidence or direct threat-trajectory support. No dispute.
